newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges court not to vacate Cochran conviction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges court not to vacate Cochran conviction.

text.p: U.S. government lawyers urged a federal appeals court Wednesday not to vacate this spring's jury conviction of former Stifel, Nicolaus & Co investment banker Robert Cochran, according to a government brief.

Susan Cox, the assistant U.S. attorney who is prosecuting the case, made the request in a 48-page brief filed with the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver in response to an appeal filed by Cochran lawyers.

Cochran lawyers had argued that the sentence should be dropped because he did not cheat the Oklahoma City Airport Trust Authority and the sisters of St. Mary Health Authority in connection with $342 million in 1992 bond deals.

They argued Cochran had no "fiduciary" relationship with the authorities and, therefore, no duty to disclose $629,000 in fees that government lawyers said he illegally pocketed on a $76.7 million airport trust issue and a $265 million healthcare authority deal.
But Cox argued in the brief that Cochran did more than just fail to disclose the fees to the authorities. He flatly "misrepresented" what they were for, she argued.
"This is your ordinary, garden-variety fraud which involved an affirmative misrepresentation" of the truth, not just a failure to disclose, Cox said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
"There is intent to deceive and, thus, a federal scheme to defraud," she said.
The jury in early May convicted the ex-Stifel vice president of eight out of 21 counts of cheating the two authorities.
U.S. District Judge Ralph Thompson sentenced Cochran in late August to over seven years in prison plus a three-year suspended sentence following the prison term.
Cochran was to report to El Reno Correctional Institution in El Reno, Oklahoma late last month. But the appeals panel on Sept 26 granted him an emergency delay of his jail term.
Judges said they needed more time to review an August 1996 decision by Judge Thompson to deny Cochran's release on bail pending his appeal.
